body.text: How do you combine all three Selçuk landmarks with Ephesus in one day?

Start at the House of the Virgin Mary at 08:30 when the hillside shrine opens, then drop 10 minutes down to Ephesus's Upper Gate so you walk downhill past the Library of Celsus to the Lower Gate. After a 15-minute photo stop at the Temple of Artemis, finish with lunch in Selçuk and the Basilica of St. John.

Because all four stops sit within a 10 km radius of Selçuk inside the [UNESCO World Heritage Ephesus](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1018/) zone, a private car or pre-arranged taxi saves you from backtracking up Mount Bülbül or walking the hot 3 km stretch between Ephesus's two gates. Check current Ephesus hours on [muze.gov.tr](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?DistId=EFS&SectionId=EFS01) before setting your morning departure.
What are the 2026 entry fees for House of the Virgin Mary (not on MuseumPass)?

In 2026, admission to the House of the Virgin Mary is 700 TL per person (roughly €13 or $15 USD), paid directly at the municipal gate. Neither MuseumPass Türkiye nor MuseumPass Aegean is accepted here because Selçuk Municipality manages site access separately from Türkiye's Ministry of Culture and Tourism.

The shrine on Mount Bülbül—documented alongside Ephesus on [muze.gov.tr](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?distid=efs&sectionid=efs02)—opens daily around 08:30 to 17:00 ([House of the Virgin Mary 2026 Guide](https://toursofephesus.com/house-of-virgin-mary-ephesus/)). By contrast, Ministry-run sites follow euro-pegged 2026 tariffs: [Ephesus Archaeological Site](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-ekle?catalogNo=WEB-ZPO01-87-009) is €40 (including the Ephesus Experience Museum), Terrace Houses are €15 extra, and [Ayasuluk / Basilica of St. John](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=STJ01&DistId=STJ) is €6 ([2026 Ephesus Entrance Fees](https://www.ephesustravelguide.com/blog/2026-ephesus-entrance-fees)).
How much remains of the Temple of Artemis today?

Very little physical structure survives at the Temple of Artemis, once one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Today visitors see marshy foundation trenches, scattered marble blocks, and a single reconstructed column topped by a stork's nest, framed by Ayasuluk Fortress and the 14th-century İsa Bey Mosque behind it.

Centuries of earthquakes, flooding, and stone quarrying—including reuse in Byzantine and Seljuk buildings—dismantled the original 127-column marble sanctuary ([Ministry of Culture & Tourism](https://www.ktb.gov.tr/EN-36251/where-to-visit.html)). Entry is free and open daily, making it a worthwhile 15-minute contextual stop before climbing Ayasuluk Hill to Emperor Justinian's 6th-century Basilica of St. John.
What dress code applies at the shrine?

There is no strictly enforced dress code at the House of the Virgin Mary gate, and women are not required to wear a headscarf. However, because the small stone chapel is an active Catholic place of worship revered by both Christians and Muslims, modest, respectful clothing covering shoulders and knees is appreciated inside.
Follow this practical checklist for a smooth Selçuk day:

items: Keep voices low inside the chapel; guides give commentary outside before entry.
Skip flash or interior photography inside the sanctuary room.
Bring a small empty bottle if you want water from the spring taps below the chapel.
Wear cushioned walking shoes with grip for Ephesus's polished marble streets.
Carry Turkish lira cash or card for the 700 TL shrine gate fee.

faq.q: Can you reach the House of the Virgin Mary by public transport from Selçuk?
faq.a: No direct public bus runs up Mount Bülbül. Most independent travelers hire a local taxi from Selçuk (about 15 minutes uphill) with waiting time included, or arrange a private driver for the full circuit.

faq.q: Is the House of the Virgin Mary wheelchair accessible?
faq.a: Yes. The path from the parking area to the chapel is paved and gently graded, and the main chapel entrance is step-free, making it one of the most accessible sites near Ephesus.

faq.q: Does the Basilica of St. John ticket include Ayasuluk Fortress?
faq.a: Yes. The €6 Ayasuluk–St. John ticket grants access to both the 6th-century basilica ruins and the restored Ayasuluk Fortress walls higher up the hill.

faq.q: Are Mass services still held at the House of the Virgin Mary?
faq.a: Yes. Daily Mass is celebrated by the resident Capuchin fathers, with a larger Sunday service typically held at 10:30 and major feast-day services on August 15.

faq.q: Is MuseumPass Aegean worth buying for this single day?
faq.a: If you only visit Ephesus (€40) and St. John's Basilica (€6), individual tickets cost €46—far less than the €95 MuseumPass Aegean. The pass only pays off if you also visit Pergamon, Pamukkale, Aphrodisias, or Bodrum within seven days.

faq.q: How far is the Temple of Artemis from the Basilica of St. John?
faq.a: They sit roughly 500 meters apart in Selçuk—an easy 8-minute walk or 2-minute drive past the historic İsa Bey Mosque.
